newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 9.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Judicial Affairs Office secretary-general has castigated Prime Minister's Office Minister Bokhin Polakula for pushing to keep the new administrative court under the control of the Council of State, saying Bokhin is naive, has breached protocol and wants only to satisfy his own desires. The minister has said the administrative court should be separate from existing courts and have its general affairs handled by the council. (THE NATION)

- Two middle-ranking police officers have been transferred to inactive posts in what sources say is a white-wash to put an end to a scandal following a major amphetamine drug bust in Nonthaburi province. The two officers were said to be among a group of policemen and four reporters who pocketed two million baht seized from an amphetamine dealer, after a raid on his apartment. (BANGKOK POST)

- Washington is expected to grant the military free use of a defence satellite following the decision to scrap the Star of Siam project. The United States is expected to approve the launch of one of four reserve satellites in low orbit following an approach said to have been ordered by Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, as defence minister. (BANGKOK POST)

- Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan says the Bank of Thailand, the Government Housing Bank and the Government Savings Bank will jointly set up a fund totalling 20 billion baht to help government and state enterprise employees purchase their houses. He says financial institutions will help set up a Resolution Trust Fund to help financially-plagued property development companies. (KRUNGTHEP THURAKIJ)

- The Securities and Exchange Commission board is expected to endorse legalised short-selling on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) when it meets today. But Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan says that short sales must be done openly, with prices of the stocks in question are higher than prevailing market prices if short-selling is to really help stabilise the SET. (BANGKOK POST)

- The government's economic team will focus on liberalisation, privatisation and scrapping useless regulations, Prime Minister Chavalit assured a meeting attended by members of foreign chambers of commerce yesterday. Economic ministers who attended the meeting also presented the government's plans for solving the country's economic problems. (BUSINESS DAY)
